decisive_items: elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal
inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis
response.rationale: A midline vermian mass with DWI high signal and elevated choline/low NAA is characteristic of hypercellular medulloblastoma; hemangioblastoma is less likely given DWI restriction and the cited absence of hemorrhage/calcification, while astrocytoma lacks the specific location and restriction evidence.

rejected.why: Only nonspecific cerebellar syndrome and T2 hyperintensity are supplied; no vermian/foramen location, DWI restriction, or MRS evidence.
